memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'It is a guilt offering; they have been guilty of wrongdoing against the LORD.'" - Lev 5:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with a summary that could easily be overlooked: wrongdoing against the LORD.

Read back through this chapter and notice how many of the offences involved other people. Failing to testify. Breaking an oath. Withholding what was due. Damaging something entrusted. These were horizontal failures, human to human.

And God calls every one of them wrongdoing against the LORD.

That is one of the most important things Scripture teaches about sin. There is no such thing as a purely private matter between you and another person. Every wrong done to a human being is also done to the God who made them and loves them.

David understood this after the worst act of his life. Having wronged Bathsheba, Uriah, and the nation, he prayed: Against you, you only, have I sinned and done what is evil in your sight (Ps 51:4). He was not dismissing the human damage. He was recognising the deepest dimension of it.

Jesus taught the same in reverse: whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me (Mtt 25:40).

How you treat people is how you treat God. There is no separating the two.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I think of my treatment of people as separate from my relationship with God?
2. Is there someone I have wronged whom I need to see as made in God's image?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for wrongs I thought were only between me and another person. Teach me to see You in how I treat everyone around me. Amen.
